Class RandomSelectorAssert<T>

java.lang.Object
org.assertj.core.api.AbstractAssert<RandomSelectorAssert<T>, RandomSelector<T>>
be.imgn.gaia.core.testing.RandomSelectorAssert<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the elements
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.assertj.core.api.Assert<RandomSelectorAssert<T>, RandomSelector<T>>, org.assertj.core.api.Descriptable<RandomSelectorAssert<T>>, org.assertj.core.api.ExtensionPoints<RandomSelectorAssert<T>, RandomSelector<T>>
public final class RandomSelectorAssert<T> extends org.assertj.core.api.AbstractAssert<RandomSelectorAssert<T>, RandomSelector<T>>
AssertJ assertions on how often a RandomSelector selects each element: the selector is asked for many elements, and the counts are compared with what the expected chances make likely. 
assertThat(rarity).selectsInProportion(Map.of("common", 70, "rare", 25, "legendary", 5));
assertThat(rarity).selectsWithItsChances();
assertThat(loot).usingRandom(new SplittableRandom(42)).inSelections(1_000_000).selectsWith(expected);

The comparison is a chi-squared test: an assertion passes when counts as far from the expected ones would come up by chance more than about once in a million tests of a correct selector. A selector that is wrong by little passes too, unless enough elements are selected to tell: with the default of 100,000 selections, chances that are off by one percent of the whole are found, and smaller differences mostly aren't.

The selections use a SplittableRandom with a fixed seed unless another source of randomness is given, so that a test passes or fails the same way each time it runs.

Since:
0.2.0
